questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass $1$ kg moves along a straight line with a velocity $v = 2x^2$. The work done by the body during displacement from $x = 0$ to $5$ m is __________ J.
questions.solution:
Given mass $m = 1$ kg and velocity $v = 2x^2$.

According to the work-energy theorem, the work done by the net force is equal to the change in kinetic energy of the body.

$W = \Delta K = K_f - K_i$

At $x = 0$ m, initial velocity $v_i = 2(0)^2 = 0$ m/s.

At $x = 5$ m, final velocity $v_f = 2(5)^2 = 50$ m/s.

Initial kinetic energy $K_i = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_i^2 = 0$ J.

Final kinetic energy $K_f = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_f^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times (50)^2 = 1250$ J.

Work done $W = 1250 - 0 = 1250$ J.

Answer: $1250$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity at which $6$ kg mass (shown in figure) strikes the ground when it is released from a height of $6$ m above the ground is __________ m/s. Assume pulley is massless and string is light and inextensible. (Take g $= 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Let the acceleration of the system be $a$ and the tension in the string be $T$.

The equations of motion for the two masses are:
$6g - T = 6a$
$T - 2g = 2a$

Adding the two equations, we get:
$4g = 8a$
$\Rightarrow a = \dfrac{4g}{8} = \dfrac{g}{2}$

Substituting $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$, the acceleration is:
$a = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5 \text{ m/s}^2$

The $6 \text{ kg}$ mass is released from rest ($u = 0$) and travels a downward distance $s = 6 \text{ m}$.

Using the kinematic equation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$:
$v^2 = 0 + 2 \times 5 \times 6$
$v^2 = 60$
$v = \sqrt{60} \approx 7.74 \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $7.74$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The rain drop of mass $1$ g, starts with zero velocity from a height of $1$ km. It hits the ground with a speed of $5$ m/s. The work done by the unknown resistive force is _______ J. (take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Using the work-energy theorem, the total work done by all forces equals the change in kinetic energy:

$W_{g} + W_{r} = \Delta K$

$mgh + W_{r} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 - 0$

Substituting the given values ($m = 10^{-3}$ kg, $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, $h = 1000$ m, $v = 5$ m/s):

$(10^{-3})(10)(1000) + W_{r} = \dfrac{1}{2}(10^{-3})(5)^2$

$10 + W_{r} = 0.0125$

$W_{r} = 0.0125 - 10 = -9.9875$ J

$W_{r} \approx -9.98$ J

Answer: $-9.98$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A smooth inclined plane ends in a vertical circular loop, as shown in the figure. A small body is released from height $h$ as shown. If the body exerts a force of three times its weight on the plane at the highest point of circle then the height $h = \alpha R$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.solution:
Let $v$ be the velocity of the body at the highest point of the circular loop.

At the highest point, the forces acting on the body are its weight $mg$ (downwards) and the normal reaction $N$ (downwards). The net downward force provides the necessary centripetal acceleration:

$N + mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{R}$

Given that the body exerts a force equal to three times its weight on the track at the highest point, we have $N = 3mg$. Substituting this into the equation:

$3mg + mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{R}$

$4mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{R} \Rightarrow v^2 = 4gR$

Applying the principle of conservation of mechanical energy between the point of release and the highest point of the loop (which is at a height of $2R$ from the bottom):

$mgh = mg(2R) + \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$

Substituting $v^2 = 4gR$ into the energy equation:

$mgh = 2mgR + \dfrac{1}{2}m(4gR)$

$mgh = 2mgR + 2mgR = 4mgR$

Therefore, $h = 4R$.

Comparing this with the given relation $h = \alpha R$, we get $\alpha = 4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $1$ kg block subjected to two simultaneous forces $(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$ N and $(3\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$ N is moved a distance of $25$ m along $(3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j})$ direction. The work done in this process is _____ J.
questions.solution:
The net force acting on the block is the vector sum of the two forces:

$\vec{F} = \vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2 = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) + (3\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}) = 5\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ N

The block is moved a distance of $25$ m along the direction of the vector $3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}$. The unit vector along this direction is:

$\hat{n} = \dfrac{3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2}} = \dfrac{3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}}{5}$

The displacement vector $\vec{s}$ is the magnitude multiplied by the unit vector:

$\vec{s} = 25 \hat{n} = 25 \left( \dfrac{3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}}{5} \right) = 15\hat{i} - 20\hat{j}$ m

The work done $W$ is the dot product of the net force and the displacement vector:

$W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{s} = (5\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) \cdot (15\hat{i} - 20\hat{j})$

$W = (5 \times 15) + (2 \times -20) + (2 \times 0)$

$W = 75 - 40 = 35$ J

Answer: $35$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass $2$ kg begins to move under the influence of time dependent force $\vec{F} = (2t\hat{i} + 6t^2\hat{j})$ N, where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are unit vectors along $x$ and $y$-axis respectively. The power produced by the force at $t = 2$ s is _____ W.
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{F} = (2t\hat{i} + 6t^2\hat{j})$ N and $m = 2$ kg.

Acceleration of the body is $\vec{a} = \dfrac{\vec{F}}{m} = \dfrac{2t\hat{i} + 6t^2\hat{j}}{2} = t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j}$ m/s$^2$.

Since the body begins to move from rest, its velocity at time $t$ is given by $\vec{v} = \int \vec{a} dt = \int (t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j}) dt = \dfrac{t^2}{2}\hat{i} + t^3\hat{j}$ m/s.

At $t = 2$ s, the force is $\vec{F} = 2(2)\hat{i} + 6(2)^2\hat{j} = 4\hat{i} + 24\hat{j}$ N.

At $t = 2$ s, the velocity is $\vec{v} = \dfrac{(2)^2}{2}\hat{i} + (2)^3\hat{j} = 2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j}$ m/s.

Power produced by the force is $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = (4\hat{i} + 24\hat{j}) \cdot (2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j})$.

$P = (4 \times 2) + (24 \times 8) = 8 + 192 = 200$ W.

Answer: $200$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spherical ball of mass $2$ kg falls from a height of $10$ m and is brought to rest after penetrating $10$ cm into sand. The average force exerted by sand on the ball is _______ N. (Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Using the work-energy theorem, the total work done on the ball is equal to its change in kinetic energy.

Since the ball starts from rest and finally comes to rest, the change in kinetic energy is zero.

$W_{\text{gravity}} + W_{\text{sand}} = \Delta K = 0$

The work done by gravity is over the total distance $h + d$, and the work done by the resistive force of the sand $F$ is over the distance $d$.

$mg(h + d) - Fd = 0$

$F = \dfrac{mg(h + d)}{d}$

Given $m = 2$ kg, $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, $h = 10$ m, and $d = 10$ cm $= 0.1$ m:

$F = \dfrac{2 \times 10 \times (10 + 0.1)}{0.1}$

$F = \dfrac{20 \times 10.1}{0.1}$

$F = 20 \times 101 = 2020$ N

Answer: $2020$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In case of vertical circular motion of a particle by a thread of length $r$ if the tension in the thread is zero at an angle $30^{\circ}$ shown in figure, the velocity at the bottom point $(A)$ of the circular path is ($g=$ gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution:
At the point where tension $T = 0$ and angle from vertical is $60°$ (i.e., $30°$ from horizontal):
$T + mg\cos 60° = \frac{mV^2}{\ell}$
Since $T = 0$:
$V^2 = \frac{g\ell}{2}$
Using mechanical energy conservation from bottom (A) to the point where $T = 0$:
$\frac{1}{2}mu^2 = mg(\ell + \ell\cos 60°) + \frac{1}{2}mV^2$
$u^2 = 2g\ell\left(1 + \frac{1}{2}\right) + \frac{g\ell}{2} = 3g\ell + \frac{g\ell}{2} = \frac{7g\ell}{2}$
$u = \sqrt{\frac{7g\ell}{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small bob $A$ of mass $m$ is attached to a massless rigid rod of length 1 m pivoted at point $P$ and kept at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with vertical as shown in figure. At distance of 1 m below point $P$, an identical bob $B$ is kept at rest on a smooth horizontal surface that extends to a circular track of radius $R$ as shown in figure. If bob $B$ just manages to complete the circular path of radius $R$ upto a point $Q$ after being hit elastically by $\operatorname{bob} A$, then radius $R$ is $\_\_\_\_$ m.
questions.solution:
Bob A swings from $60°$ to vertical. Height drop $h = l(1-\cos 60°) = 1 \times 0.5 = 0.5$ m.
Velocity of A at bottom: $v_A = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.5} = \sqrt{10}$ m/s.
Elastic collision between equal masses: B gets $v_B = \sqrt{10}$ m/s, A stops.
For B to just complete circular loop: $v_B^2 = 5gR$.
$10 = 5 \times 10 \times R \Rightarrow R = \frac{1}{5}$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: An object moves from position $r_{1}$ to position $r_{2}$ under a conservative force field $\vec{F}$. The work done by the force is $W=-\int_{r_{1}}^{r_{2}} \vec{F} \cdot \overrightarrow{d r}$.
Statement II: Any object moving from one location to another location can follow infinite number of paths. Therefore, the amount of work done by the object changes with the path it follows for a conservative force.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
Statement I:
The work done by a force $\vec{F}$ during a displacement from $\vec{r}_1$ to $\vec{r}_2$ is defined as $W = \int_{r_1}^{r_2} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$.
The expression given in the statement, $W = -\int_{r_1}^{r_2} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$, is the definition of the change in potential energy ($\Delta U = -W$), not the work done by the force itself.
Thus, Statement I is false.

Statement II:
By definition, a conservative force is one for which the work done in moving an object between two points is independent of the path taken.
It only depends on the initial and final positions.
Therefore, the claim that work done changes with the path for a conservative force is false.

Since both statements are false, the correct option is (1).

By definition, a conservative force is one for which the work done in moving an object between two points is independent of the path taken.
It only depends on the initial and final positions.
Therefore, the claim that work done changes with the path for a conservative force is false.

Since both statements are false, the correct option is (1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass 2 kg is moving along $x$-direction such that its displacement as function of time is given by $x(t)=\alpha t^{2}+\beta t+\gamma \mathrm{m}$, where $\alpha=1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}, \beta=1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $\gamma=1 \mathrm{~m}$. The work done on the body during the time interval $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$ to $t=3 \mathrm{~s}$, is $\_\_\_\_$ J.
questions.solution:
Given $x(t) = t^2 + t + 1$, with $m = 2$ kg, find work from $t = 2$ s to $t = 3$ s.

Velocity: $v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = 2t + 1$
At $t = 2$ s: $v_i = 2(2) + 1 = 5$ m/s
At $t = 3$ s: $v_f = 2(3) + 1 = 7$ m/s

Using the work-energy theorem:
$W = \Delta KE = \frac{1}{2}m(v_f^2 - v_i^2) = \frac{1}{2}(2)(7^2 - 5^2) = 1(49 - 25) = 24$ J

questions.q: Potential energy ($V$) versus distance ($x$) is given by the graph. Rank various regions as per the magnitudes of the force (F) acting on a particle from high to low.
questions.solution:
Force is related to potential energy by $F = -\frac{dV}{dx}$.
Magnitude of force $|F| = \left|\frac{dV}{dx}\right|$ = |slope of V-x graph|
From graph coordinates: A(1, 0), B(1.5, 1), C(2, 4), D(4, 4), E(5, 3)
$|F_{AB}| = \frac{1-0}{1.5-1} = 2$
$|F_{BC}| = \frac{4-1}{2-1.5} = 6$
$|F_{CD}| = \frac{4-4}{4-2} = 0$
$|F_{DE}| = \frac{|3-4|}{5-4} = 1$
Ranking: $F_{BC} > F_{AB} > F_{DE} > F_{CD}$

questions.q: A block of mass 2 kg is attached to one end of a massless spring whose other end is fixed at a wall. The spring-mass system moves on a frictionless horizontal table. The spring's natural length is 2 m and spring constant is $200 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$. The block is pushed such that the length of the spring becomes 1 m and then released. At distance $\mathrm{x} \mathrm{m}(\mathrm{x} \lt 2)$ from the wall. the speed of the block will be :
questions.solution:
Given, Natural length of spring $=2 \mathrm{~m}$
Initial compression in spring $\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)=1 \mathrm{~m}$
Final compression in spring $\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{f}}\right)=(2-\mathrm{x}) \mathrm{m}$
Using energy conservation
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{f}} \\ & 0+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Kx}_{\mathrm{i}}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Kx}_{\mathrm{f}}^2 \\ & \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~K}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2-\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{f}}^2\right) \\ & \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times \mathrm{v}^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 200 \times\left(1^2-(2-\mathrm{x})^2\right) \\ & \mathrm{v}^2=100\left[1-(2-\mathrm{x})^2\right] \\ & \mathrm{v}=10\left[1-(2-\mathrm{x})^2\right]^{1 / 2}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An object of mass 1000 g experiences a time dependent force $\vec{F}=\left(2 t \hat{i}+3 t^2 \hat{j}\right) N$. The power generated by the force at time $t$ is :
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=(2 t \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t} \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \mathrm{N} \\ & \mathrm{m}=1000 \mathrm{gm}=1 \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~F}}=m \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=2 \mathrm{t} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{j} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 t \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}\end{aligned}$
$\vec{v}=t^2 \hat{i}+t^3 \hat{j}$
Power, $\mathrm{P}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}$
$\begin{aligned} & P=\left(2 t \hat{i}+3 t^2 \hat{j}\right) \cdot\left(t^2 \hat{i}+t^3 \hat{j}\right) \\ & P=\left(2 t^3+3 t^5\right) W\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A block of mass 25 kg is pulled along a horizontal surface by a force at an angle $45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The friction coefficient between the block and the surface is 0.25. The displacement of 5 m of the block is:
questions.solution:
Block travels with uniform velocity
So $\quad \mathrm{a}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~F} \cos 45^{\circ}=$ friction
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}=\mu\left[\mathrm{mg}-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}\right] \\ & \frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}=0.25\left[25 \times 9.8-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\sqrt{2}}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 1.25 \frac{\mathrm{~F}}{\sqrt{2}}=61.25 \\ & \mathrm{~F}=\frac{61.25 \times \sqrt{2}}{1.25}=49 \sqrt{2} \\ & \mathrm{~W}_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathrm{FS} \cos 45^{\circ} \\ &=49 \sqrt{2} \times 5 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=245 \mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle is released from height $S$ above the surface of the earth. At certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of the earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively.
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{V}^2=0+2 \mathrm{~g}(\mathrm{~S}-\mathrm{x}) \\ & \mathrm{V}^2=2 \mathrm{~g}(\mathrm{~S}-\mathrm{x})
\end{aligned}$
At B, Potential energy $=m g x$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{mgx}=3 \times \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2 \\ & \mathrm{gx}=\frac{3}{2} \times 2 \mathrm{~g}(\mathrm{~S}-\mathrm{x}) \\ & 4 \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{S} \\ & \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{S}}{4}
\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~g} \times \frac{3 \mathrm{~S}}{4}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{gS}}{2}}$

questions.q: A piston of mass $M$ is hung from a massless spring whose restoring force law goes as $\mathrm{F}=-\mathrm{kx}^3$, where k is the spring constant of appropriate dimension. The piston separates the vertical chamber into two parts, where the bottom part is filled with ' $n$ ' moles of an ideal gas. An external work is done on the gas isothermally (at a constant temperature T) with the help of a heating filament (with negligible volume) mounted in lower part of the chamber, so that the piston goes up from a height $\mathrm{L}_0$ to $\mathrm{L}_1$, the total energy delivered by the filament is (Assume spring to be in its natural length before heating)
questions.solution:
Using WET
Total energy supplied $=$ gravitational potential energy + spring potential energy + work done by gas
$\begin{aligned}
& \operatorname{Mg} \quad\left(L_1-L_0\right)+\int_{L_0}^{L_1} k^3 d x+n R T \ell n \\ & {\left[\frac{L_1 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~L}_0 \mathrm{~A}}\right]+\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{ext}}=0} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~K}}{4}\left[\mathrm{x}^4\right]_{\mathrm{L}_0}^{\mathrm{L}_1}+\operatorname{Mg}\left(\mathrm{L}_1-\mathrm{L}_0\right)+\int_{\mathrm{L}_0}^{\mathrm{L}_1} k x^3 d x+n R T \ell n
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & {\left[\frac{L_1}{L_0}\right]+\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{ext}}=0} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{k}}{4}\left(\mathrm{~L}_1^4-\mathrm{L}_0^4\right)+\operatorname{Mg} \quad\left(\mathrm{L}_1-\mathrm{L}_0\right)+\mathrm{nRT} \ell \mathrm{n} \\ & {\left[\frac{\mathrm{L}_1}{\mathrm{~L}_0}\right]+\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{ext}}=0} \\ & \mathrm{~W}_{\mathrm{ext}}=\frac{\mathrm{k}}{4}\left(\mathrm{~L}_1^4-\mathrm{L}_0^4\right)+\operatorname{Mg}\left(\mathrm{L}_1-\mathrm{L}_0\right)+\mathrm{nRT} \ell \mathrm{n}\left[\frac{\mathrm{L}_1}{\mathrm{~L}_0}\right]\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sand dropper drops sand of mass $m(t)$ on a conveyer belt at a rate proportional to the square root of speed $(v)$ of the belt, i.e. $\frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto \sqrt{v}$. If P is the power delivered to run the belt at constant speed then which of the following relationship is true?
questions.solution:
Power $=\vec{F} \cdot \vec{V}$
and $F=\frac{d p}{d t}=$ Rate of change of linear momentum
$F=V \cdot \frac{d m}{d t}=K_1 V^{\frac{3}{2}}, K$ is constant
Power $(P)=\left(K V^{\frac{3}{2}}\right) \cdot(V)$=K V^{\frac{5}{2}}$

So, $P^2 \propto V^5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $\mathbf{A}$ and the other is labelled as Reason $\mathbf{R}$
Assertion A: In a central force field, the work done is independent of the path chosen.
Reason R: Every force encountered in mechanics does not have an associated potential energy.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are true but $\mathbf{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$
Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are true and $\mathbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$
questions.solution:
Assertion is correct as central forces are conservative in nature, i.e. work done is independent of path.

Reason is true as some forces in mechanics like, friction are non-conservative because work done depends on path and only conservative forces have an associated potential energy.
Also, reason does not explain assertion.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \times 100+0=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mV}_{\mathrm{B}}^2+\mathrm{mg}\left(\mathrm{R}-\frac{\mathrm{R} \sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\ & 100=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}^2+2 \mathrm{gR}\left(1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right] \\ & \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}^2=100-20(2-\sqrt{3}) \\ & \left.\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}^2=60+20 \sqrt{3}\right) \\ & \mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mV}_{\mathrm{B}}^2=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{2}(60+20 \sqrt{3}) \\ & \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}(100)=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mV} \\ & 2 \\ & 100=\mathrm{mg}\left(\frac{3 \mathrm{R}}{2}\right) \\ & 100 \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{C}}^2=60 \\ & \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{C}}^2=40 \\ & \mathrm{~K} . \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mV} \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{C}}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}(40) \\ & \mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{60+20 \sqrt{3}}{40}=\frac{3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{3+\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$

Initial momentum is zero.
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Hence }\left|\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}\right|=\left|\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}\right| \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \frac{(\mathrm{KE})_{\mathrm{A}}}{(\mathrm{KE})_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}_{\mathrm{A}} \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}^2}{\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}^2}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}} \\ & \frac{(\mathrm{KE})_{\mathrm{B}}}{(\mathrm{KE})_{\mathrm{A}}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{i}} & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}(100)^2 \\ \mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{f}} & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}(40)^2 \\ \% \text{ loss } & =\frac{\left|\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{i}}\right|}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{i}}} \times 100 \\ & =\frac{\left|\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}(40)^2-\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}(100)^2\right|}{\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}(100)^2} \times 100 \\ & =\frac{|1600-100 \times 100|}{100}=84 \%\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time $\mathrm{t}$ is proportional to :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & P=\operatorname{constant} \Rightarrow \mathrm{FV}=\text{ constant } \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{m} \frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dt}} \mathrm{V}=\text{ constant } \\ & \int_0^{\mathrm{V}} \mathrm{VdV}=(\mathrm{C}) \int_0^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt} \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{2}\right)=\mathrm{Ct} \\ & \mathrm{V} \propto \mathrm{t}^{1 / 2} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{ds}}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto \mathrm{t}^{1 / 2} \\ & \int_0^{\mathrm{S}} \mathrm{ds}=\mathrm{K} \int_0^{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{t}^{1 / 2} \mathrm{dt} \\ & \mathrm{S}=\mathrm{K} \times \frac{2}{3} \mathrm{t}^{3 / 2} \\ & \mathrm{ S} \propto \mathrm{t}^{3 / 2}\end{aligned} \therefore$ displacement is proportional to $(\mathrm{t})^{3 / 2}$

questions.q:
A body of $m \mathrm{~kg}$ slides from rest along the curve of vertical circle from point $A$ to $B$ in friction less path. The velocity of the body at $B$ is:
$\text{ (given, } R=14 \mathrm{~m}, g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \text{ and } \sqrt{2}=1.4 \text{ ) }$
questions.solution:
Apply W.E.T. from A to B
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{mg}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{A}} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{mg} \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{2}}+\mathrm{R}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}^2-0\left\{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}=0 \text{ rest }\right\} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{mgR} \frac{(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{B}^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{gR} \frac{2(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{10 \times 14 \times 2(2.4)}{1.4}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\
& \Rightarrow 21.9=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If a rubber ball falls from a height $h$ and rebounds upto the height of $h / 2$. The percentage loss of total energy of the initial system as well as velocity ball before it strikes the ground, respectively, are :

\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body of mass $2kg$ begins to move under the action of a time dependent force given by $\overset{\to}{F} = \left(6t\overset{^}{i} + 6{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)N$. The power developed by the force at the time $t$ is given by:
questions.solution:
Given: $\overset{\to}{F} = \left(6t\overset{^}{i} + 6{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)N$

Now, $\overset{\to}{F} = m\overset{\to}{a} = \left(6t\overset{^}{i} + 6{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{F}m = \left(3t\overset{^}{i} + 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)$

Hence, velocity $\overset{\to}{v} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{t}\overset{\to}{a}dt = \dfrac{3{t}^{2}}{2}\overset{^}{i} + {t}^{3}\overset{^}{j}$

Required power, $P = \overset{\to}{F} . \overset{\to}{v} = \left(9{t}^{3} + 6{t}^{5}\right)W$

questions.q: An artillery piece of mass ${M}_{1}$ fires a shell of mass ${M}_{2}$ horizontally. Instantaneously after the firing, the ratio of kinetic energy of the artillery and that of the shell is :
questions.solution:
As linear momentum will be conserved, $\left|\overset{⇀}{p}1\right| = \left|\overset{⇀}{p}2\right|$

Now, kinetic energy can be written as $KE = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2M}$.

Also $p$ is the same for both masses. We can write,

$KE ∝ \dfrac{1}{m}$

$⇒ \dfrac{K{E}_{1}}{K{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2{M}_{1}}}{\dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2{M}_{2}}} = \dfrac{{M}_{2}}{{M}_{1}}$

questions.q: A solid circular disc of mass $50kg$ rolls along a horizontal floor so that its center of mass has a speed of $0 . 4m{s}^{- 1}$. The absolute value of work done on the disc to stop it is ______ $J$.
questions.solution:
Using work-energy theorem, we get

$W = ∆ KE$

$⇒ W = 0 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ W = 0 - \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{{K}^{2}}{{R}^{2}}\right)$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2} \times 50 \times 0 . {4}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = - 6J$

Absolute work $= + 6J$

Therefore, required value of $W = 6J$

questions.q: The bob of a pendulum was released from a horizontal position. The length of the pendulum is $10m$. If it dissipates $10 %$ of its initial energy against air resistance, the speed with which the bob arrives at the lowest point is: [Use, $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$ ]
questions.solution:
Given the length of the pendulum is $ℓ = 10m$.

The initial potential energy of the pendulum at the horizontal position is given by

$U = mgℓ . . . \left(1\right)$

The final kinetic energy of the pendulum at the lowermost position is given by

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

So, from equations (1) and (2), it follows that

$\dfrac{9}{10}mgℓ = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{9}{10} \times 10 \times 10 = \dfrac{1}{2}{v}^{2} ⇒ {v}^{2} = 180 ⇒ v = \sqrt{180} = 6\sqrt{5}m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A ball suspended by a thread swings in a vertical plane so that its magnitude of acceleration in the extreme position and lowest position are equal. The angle $( \theta )$ of thread deflection in the extreme position will be :
questions.solution:
At the lowermost point, there is no tangential force on the ball. Thus, there exists no tangential acceleration at the bottommost point, only the centripetal acceleration survives.

On the other hand, in the extreme position of the ball, there is no centripetal acceleration as the ball becomes momentarily at rest at that position. Here, only tangential acceleration survives.

Thus, with respect to the figure above, equating the kinetic energy at the bottommost point to the potential energy at the extreme point, we have
$\dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} = mgl ( 1 - cos\theta ) ⇒ \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{l} = 2g ( 1 - cos\theta ) . . . \left(1\right)

Now,$ the $net acceleration \left({a}_{t}\right) at the extreme point can be written as

${a}_{t} = gsin\theta . . . $\left(2\right)$

According to the given problem, it follows that for the two positions of the ball,

${a}_{t} = \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{l} . . . \left(3\right)

$gsin\theta = 2g ( 1 - cos\theta ) ⇒ 2sin$\dfrac{\theta}{2}$cos$\dfrac{\theta}{2} =$4$\sin^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}$ ⇒ tan$\dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \theta = 2$\tan^{- 1}$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

questions.q: A car accelerates from rest of $um{s}^{- 1}$. The energy spent in this process is $EJ$. The energy required to accelerate the car from $um{s}^{- 1}$ to $2um{s}^{- 1}$ is $nEJ$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of a moving particle is given by

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}m{u}^{2} . . . ( 1 )$

When the final velocity of the particle becomes twice the initial velocity, the kinetic energy of the particle can be written as

$\begin{cases}nE & = & \dfrac{1}{2}m\left\{( 2u{)}^{2} - {u}^{2}\right\} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(3{u}^{2}\right) . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and solve to calculate the value of $n$.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{nE}{E} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}m\left(3{u}^{2}\right)}{\dfrac{1}{2}m{u}^{2}} \\ & ⇒ & n = 3\end{cases}$

questions.solution:
The work done in raising the water is $W = mgh$.

Power is $P = \dfrac{W}{t}$

Let the powers of both the motors be ${P}_{1} \text{ and } {P}_{2}$ respectively.

Hence, the ratio of the powers is,

$\dfrac{{P}_{1}}{{P}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{300 \times g \times 100}{5 \times 60}}{\dfrac{50 \times g \times 100}{2 \times 60}} = \dfrac{60}{25} ⇒ \dfrac{3\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x} + 1} = 2 . 4$

$⇒ 3\sqrt{x} = 2 . 4\sqrt{x} + 2 . 4$

$⇒ x = 16$

questions.q: A body of mass $( 5 \pm 0 . 5 ) kg$ is moving with a velocity of $( 20 \pm 0 . 4 ) m{s}^{- 1} .$ Its kinetic energy will be
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy is given by,

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

Differentiating the above equation,

$dK = \dfrac{1}{2} ( {v}^{2}dm + 2mvdv )$

Dividing by $K$,

$⇒ \dfrac{dK}{K} = \dfrac{dm}{m} + \dfrac{2dv}{v}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dK}{1000} = \dfrac{0 . 5}{5} + \dfrac{2 \times 0 . 4}{20}$

$⇒ dK = 100 + 40 = 140$

$⇒ KE = ( 1000 \pm 140 ) J$

questions.q: To maintain a speed of $80km{h}^{- 1}$ by a bus of mass $500kg$ on a plane rough road for $4km$ distance, the work done by the engine of the bus will be _____ $kJ$. [The coefficient of friction between tyre of bus and road is $0 . 04$]
questions.solution:
It is given,

$v = 80km{h}^{- 1}$

$m = 500kg$

$S = 4km$

$\mu = 0 . 04$

The power due to friction is

${P}_{f} = Fv$ where $F = \mumg$

$= \left(\left(0 . 04\right)\left(500 \times 9 . 8\right) \times 80 \times \dfrac{5}{18}\right)W$

Hence, the work done by the engine in overcoming the friction is

$W = {P}_{f}t = {P}_{f}\dfrac{d}{v}$

$⇒ W = 20 \times 9 . 8 \times 80 \times \dfrac{5}{18} \times \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{3}}{80 \times \dfrac{5}{18}} = 784kJ$

questions.q:
A hollow spherical ball of uniform density rolls up a curved surface with an initial velocity $3m{s}^{- 1}$ (as shown in figure). Maximum height with respect to the initial position covered by it will be _____ $cm$
(take, $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
The total kinetic energy of the ball at the bottom of the curve can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}K & = & \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}M{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}M{\left(R\omega\right)}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}M{v}^{2}\left[∵ v = \omegaR\right] \\ & = & \dfrac{5}{6}M{v}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the potential energy acquired by the ball when it attains the maximum height is given by

$U = Mgh . . . \left(2\right)$

Equate equation (1) and (2) and simplify to obtain the required height.

$\begin{cases}Mgh & = & \dfrac{5}{6}M{v}^{2} \\ & ⇒ & h = \dfrac{5{v}^{2}}{6g} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required height attained by the ball.
$\begin{cases}h & = & \dfrac{5 \times {\left(3m{s}^{- 1}\right)}^{2}}{6 \times 10m{s}^{- 2}} \\ & = & 0 . 75m \times \dfrac{100cm}{1m} \\ & = & 75cm\end{cases}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The momentum of a body is increased by $50 %$. The percentage increase in the kinetic energy of the body is_$_______ % .$
questions.solution:
The relation of kinetic energy and momentum is given by

$K = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m}$

The new value of momentum is $p ' = 1 . 5p$

The new value of kinetic energy is

$⇒ K ' = \dfrac{{\left(1 . 5p\right)}^{2}}{2m} = 2 . 25K$

Hence, the percentage increase in kinetic energy is

$\dfrac{K ' - K}{K} \times 100 = \dfrac{2 . 25K - K}{K} = 125 %$

If the ratio of velocities of the body just before and after hitting ground is $4$, then percentage loss in kinetic energy of the body is $\dfrac{x}{4}$. The value of $x$ is _____.

questions.solution:
At first the block is pulled to a distance ${x}_{0} = 10cm$(extreme position).

Potential energy of block is ${U}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2}$ and kinetic energy os block, ${K}_{i} = 0$.

Now, when the block is at distance $5cm$.

Potential energy is ${U}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}k{\left(\dfrac{{x}_{0}}{2}\right)}^{2}$ and kinetic energy is ${K}_{f} = 0 . 25J$

Total energy of block will be conserved, so

$\dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2} + 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2}4 + 0 . 25$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}k\dfrac{3}{100} = 1 ⇒ k = \dfrac{200}{3}N{m}^{- 1}$

$= 67N{m}^{- 1}$

Given, the force exerted on the object is

The formula to calculate the work done $\left(W\right)$ by the force in moving the object from a position ${y}_{1}$ to another position ${y}_{2}$ can be written as

questions.q: A small particle moves to position $5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ from its initial position $2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$ under the action of force $5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}N$. The value of work done will be ______ $J$.
questions.solution:
Work done by a constant force is given by $W = Force\left(\overset{\to}{F}\right) \cdot Displacement\left(\overset{\to}{r}\right)$, where, $\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{r}2 - \overset{\to}{r}1$

Given here, $\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} = 5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{r}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

So, $W = \overset{\to}{F} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{r}2 - \overset{\to}{r}1\right)$

$= ( 5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot \left[( 5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) - ( 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k} )\right]$

$⇒ W = 40J$

questions.q: A lift of mass $M = 500kg$ is descending with speed of $2m{s}^{- 1}$. Its supporting cable begins to slip thus allowing it to fall with a constant acceleration of $2m{s}^{- 2}$. The kinetic energy of the lift at the end of fall through to a distance of $6m$ will be ______ $kJ$.
questions.solution:
Given, $u = 2m{s}^{- 1}, a = 2m{s}^{- 2}, s = 6m$

Using kinematics third equation of motion, final speed of lift is ${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2as$

$⇒ v = {2}^{2} + 2\left(2\right)\left(6\right)$

$= 4 + 24 = 28m{s}^{- 1}$

Now, kinetic energy of the lift is $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} ( 500 ) 28$

$= 7000J$

$= 7kJ$

questions.q: A body of mass $2kg$ is initially at rest. It starts moving unidirectionally under the influence of a source of constant power $P$. Its displacement in $4s$ is $\dfrac{1}{3}{\alpha}^{2}\sqrt{P}m$. The value of $\alpha$ will be ______.
questions.solution:
Energy provided will be used to increase kinetic energy of the body. Therefore,

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{V}^{2} = Pt$

$V = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Pt}{m}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Pt}{m}} ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{x}dx = \sqrt{\dfrac{2P}{m}}{∫}_{0}^{4}t\dfrac{1}{2}dt$

$⇒ x = \sqrt{\dfrac{2P}{m}}\dfrac{2}{3}{\left[t\dfrac{3}{2}\right]}_{0}^{4}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{16\sqrt{P}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 16\sqrt{P}$

Hence, required value of $\alpha = 4$.

questions.q:
Identify the correct statements from the following:

(A) Work done by a man in lifting a bucket out of a well by means of a rope tied to the bucket is negative

(B) Work done by gravitational force in lifting a bucket out of a well by a rope tied to the bucket is negative

(C) Work done by friction on a body sliding down an inclined plane is positive

(D) Work done by an applied force on a body moving on a rough horizontal plane with uniform velocity is zero

(E) Work done by the air resistance on an oscillating pendulum is negative

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Work done is given by, $W = Fscos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the force and the displacement.

case(A): Direction of force and displacement both are in the same direction and hence work done will be positive. Hence, wrong.

case(B): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, correct.

case(C): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, wrong.

case(D): Direction of force and displacement both are in the same direction and hence work done will be positive. Hence, wrong.

case(E): Direction of force and displacement both are in the opposite direction and hence work done will be negative. Hence, correct.

questions.q: A $0 . 4kg$ mass takes $8s$ to reach ground when dropped from a certain height $P$ above surface of earth. The loss of potential energy in the last second of fall is ______ $J$. [Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$]
questions.solution:
Displacement in ${n}^{th}$ second is given by ${S}_{n} = u + \dfrac{a}{2}\left(2n - 1\right)$

Here, displacement is 8th second is

${S}_{8} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times ( 2 \times 8 - 1 )$

$⇒ {S}_{8} = 75m$

Loss of potential energy is

$\DeltaU = mg{S}_{8} = 0 . 4 \times 10 \times 75$

$⇒ \DeltaU = 300J$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object of mass $m$ initially at rest on a smooth horizontal plane starts moving under the action of force $F = 2N$. In the process of its linear motion, the angle $\theta$ (as shown in figure) between the direction of force and horizontal varies as $\theta = kx$, where $k$ is a constant and $x$ is the distance covered by the object from its initial position. The expression of kinetic energy of the object will be $E = \dfrac{n}{k}sin\theta$. The value of $n$ is ______.
questions.solution:
As seen in the free body diagram of the object, normal force $N$, weight $mg$ and force in parallel and perpendicular directions are acting.

Using Newton's law of motion

Along horizontal direction, $Fcos\theta = ma$

$⇒ 2cos ( kx ) = mv\dfrac{d v}{d x}$

Integrating the above relation, we have

${∫}_{0}^{v}v d v = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}cos ( kx ) d x$

$⇒ \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{2}{k}sinkx$

Thus, kinetic energy of the object will be $K . E . = \dfrac{2}{k}sin\theta$

Thus, the value of $n = 2$.

questions.q: A body of mass $1kg$ begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\overset{\to}{F} = \left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)N$, where $\overset{^}{i}$ and $\overset{^}{j}$ are the unit vectors along $x$ and $y$ axis. The power developed by above force, at the time $t = 2s$, will be _______$W$.
questions.solution:
Given, $\overset{\to}{F} = \left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)N$ and $m = 1kg$

Now, we can write from Newton's second law, $\overset{\to}{F} = m\overset{\to}{a} = m\dfrac{d \overset{\to}{v}}{d t}$

Then, $d \overset{\to}{v} = \left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) d t$

Integrating the above,

${∫}_{0}^{v} d \overset{\to}{v} = {∫}_{0}^{t}\left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) d t ⇒ \overset{\to}{v} = \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{2}\overset{^}{i} + {t}^{3}\overset{^}{j}$

Now, power developed by the force is $P = \overset{\to}{F} \cdot \overset{\to}{v} = \left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{{t}^{2}}{2}\overset{^}{i} + {t}^{3}\overset{^}{j}\right)$

$= \left(\dfrac{{t}^{3}}{2} + 3{t}^{5}\right)$

At $t = 2s$, power is $P = \left(\dfrac{{2}^{3}}{2} + 3{\left(2\right)}^{5}\right) = 4 + \left(3 \times 32\right) = 100W$

questions.q: A spherical body of mass $2kg$ starting from rest acquires a kinetic energy of $10000J$ at the end of ${5}^{\text{th}}$ second. The force acted on the body is _____ $N$.
questions.solution:
Given kinetic energy, $\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = 10000J$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times {v}^{2} = 10000$

$⇒ {v}^{2} = 10000$

$⇒ v = 100m{s}^{- 1}$

Also,

$⇒ v = at = a \times 5 = 100$

$⇒ a = 20m{s}^{- 2}$

Therefore, force acting

$F = ma = 2 \times 20 = 40N$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If momentum of a body is increased by $20 %$, then its kinetic energy increases by :
questions.solution:
A body of mass $m$, moving with momentum $p$ and kinetic energy $K$ are related as follows,
$K = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m}$.
As the momentum of the body is increased by $20 %$, then its momentum becomes,
$\left(p + \dfrac{20}{100}p\right) = 1 . 2p$
and the mass of the body remains unchanged. So, kinetic energy is directly related to the square of momentum.

Hence, new kinetic energy $\left({K}^{'}\right)$ will be,
${K}^{'} = \dfrac{{\left(1 . 2p\right)}^{2}}{2m}$

${K}^{'} = 1 . 44K$.

So, the percentage change in kinetic energy
$= \dfrac{{K}^{'} - K}{K} \times 100$
$= \dfrac{1 . 44K - K}{K} \times 100$
$= \left(1 . 44 - 1\right) \times 100$
$= 44 %$.

questions.q: A bullet of mass $200g$ having initial kinetic energy $90J$ is shot inside a long swimming pool as shown in the figure. If it's kinetic energy reduces to $40J$ within $1s$, the minimum length of the pool, the bullet has to travel so that it completely comes to rest is
questions.solution:
Let us assume that the motion of the bullet is of constant retardation inside the water.

Initial kinetic energy $\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2} = 90J$

$⇒ {v}_{0} = 30m{s}^{- 1}$

Let the retardation is $a$, then after $1s$

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(30 - a \times 1\right)}^{2} = 40J$

$⇒ 30 - a = 20$

$⇒ a = 10m{s}^{- 2}$

Stopping distance for the constant retardation is given by,

$l = \dfrac{{u}^{2}}{2a} = \dfrac{{30}^{2}}{20} = 45m$.

Therefore, the minimum length of the pool required is $45m$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass '$m$' (as shown in figure) moving with kinetic energy $E$ compresses a spring through a distance $25cm$ when, its speed is halved. The value of spring constant of used spring will be $nEN{m}^{- 1}$ for $n =$_____.
questions.solution:
Using work $-$ energy theorem

${W}_{net} = ∆ KE$

${W}_{net} = \left({K}_{f} - {K}_{i}\right)$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2}K{x}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} ⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2}K{x}^{2} = \dfrac{E}{4} - E$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}K{x}^{2} = \dfrac{3E}{4} ⇒ K = \dfrac{3E}{2{x}^{2}}$

$⇒ K = \dfrac{3E}{2 \times {\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2}} = 24EN{m}^{- 1}$

Thus, the value of $n = 24$.

questions.q:
Two inclined planes are placed as shown in figure.
A block is projected from the Point $A$ of inclined plane $AB$ along its surface with a velocity just sufficient to carry it to the top Point $B$ at a height $10m$. After reaching the Point $B$ the block slides down on inclined plane $BC$. Time it takes to reach to the point $C$ from point $A$ is $t\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)s$. The value of t is _____ (use $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
From energy conservation at point $A$ and $B$,

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2} = mgh$

$⇒ {v}_{0} = \sqrt{gh} = \sqrt{10 \times 10}$

$⇒ {v}_{0} = 10\sqrt{2}m{s}^{- 1}$

For $A \to B$

At $B, v = 0$

Acceleration of a particle moving on a smooth incline is $gsin\theta$. Therefore, along $AB$, $a = - gsin45 ° = \dfrac{- 10}{\sqrt{2}}m{s}^{- 2}$.

Using equation of motion,

$v = u + a{t}_{1}$

$0 = 10\sqrt{2} - \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{2}}{t}_{1} ⇒ {t}_{1} = 2s$

For $B \to C$

Using second equation of motion,

$s = u{t}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{10}{sin30 °} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(10sin30 °\right){t}_{2}^{2}$

${t}_{2} = 2\sqrt{2}s$

So total time $T = {t}_{1} + {t}_{2}$= 2\sqrt{2} + 2$

$= 2\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)s$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Sand is being dropped from a stationary dropper at a rate of $0 . 5kg{s}^{- 1}$ on a conveyor belt moving with a velocity of $5m{s}^{- 1}$. The power needed to keep belt moving with the same velocity will be
questions.solution:
When the sand is dropped on the conveyor belt its velocity will become equal to that of the conveyor. Therefore, $v = 5m{s}^{- 1}$.

The force required to keep the conveyor belt moving will be equal to the gain in the momentum by the sand per second.

$⇒ F = \dfrac{d m}{d t}v ⇒ F = 0 . 5 \times 5 = 2 . 5N$

Now the power required to keep the conveyor belt moving will be,

$P = Fv ⇒ P = 2 . 5 \times 5 = 12 . 5W .$

questions.q: A stone tide to a string of length $L$ is whirled in a vertical circle with the other end of the string at the centre. At a certain instant of time, the stone is at its lowest position and has a speed $u$. The magnitude of change in its velocity, as it reaches a position where the string is horizontal, is $\sqrt{x\left({u}^{2} - gL\right)}$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
Applying conservation of mechanical energy at the point $A and B$, we get$\dfrac{1}{2}m{u}^{2} + 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + mgL$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{{u}^{2} - 2gL}$

Now in vector form. $\overset{\to}{v}i = u\overset{^}{i} and \overset{\to}{v}f = v\overset{^}{j}$

Therefore, change in velocity will be,$∆ \overset{\to}{V} = v\overset{^}{j} - u\overset{^}{i} and \left|\Delta\overset{\to}{V}\right| = \sqrt{{u}^{2} + {v}^{2}}$

$⇒ \DeltaV = \sqrt{{u}^{2} + \left({u}^{2} - 2gL\right)}$

$= \sqrt{2\left({u}^{2} - gL\right)}$

Hence, $x = 2$

questions.q:
A rolling wheel of $12kg$ is on an inclined plane at position $P$ and connected to a mass of $3kg$ through a string of fixed length and pulley as shown in figure.
Consider $PR$ as friction free surface.
The velocity of centre of mass of the wheel when it reaches at the bottom $Q$ of the inclined plane $PQ$ will be $\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{xgh}m{s}^{- 1}$. The value of $x$ (rounded off to the nearest integer) is _____.
questions.solution:
If we take the wheel as a ring then its moment of inertia will be, $I = M{r}^{2}$.

Using mechanical energy conservation,

$Mgh - mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2} ⇒ 12gh - 3gh = \dfrac{1}{2}3{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}12{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}12{r}^{2}\dfrac{{v}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}$

$⇒ 9gh = \dfrac{15{v}^{2} + 12{v}^{2}}{2}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}gh} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3}gh}$

Therefore, $x = \dfrac{8}{3} ≃ 3$

$⇒ x = \left(\dfrac{8P}{9m}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}t\dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q: Consider a force $\overset{\to}{F} = - x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}$ . The work done by this force in moving a particle from point $A\left(1,0\right)$ to $B\left(0,1\right)$ along the line segment is : (all quantities are in SI units)
questions.solution:
It is given that a force $\overset{\to}{F} = - x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}$ acts on a particle. The particle is moved from point $A\left(1, 0\right)$ to $B\left(0, 1\right)$ along the line segment.

Work done by a variable force on the particle,
$W = ∫ \overset{\to}{F} \cdot \overset{\to}{dr} = ∫ \overset{\to}{F} \cdot \left(dx\overset{^}{i} + dy\overset{^}{j}\right)$
(In two dimension, $\overset{\to}{dr} = dx\overset{^}{i} + dy\overset{^}{j}$
and it is given $\overset{\to}{F} = - x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}$)

$W = ∫ \left(- x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}\right) \cdot \left(dx\overset{^}{i} + dy\overset{^}{j}\right)$

$= ∫ - xdx + ydy = ∫ - xdx + ∫ ydy$.
As the particle is displaced from $A\left(1, 0\right)$ to $B\left(0, 1\right)$, $x$ varies from $1$ to $0$ and $y$ varies from $0$ to $1$.
So, work will be,

$W = - {∫}_{1}^{0}xdx + {∫}_{0}^{1}ydy = - {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{1}^{0} + {\left[\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(0 + {\left(1\right)}^{2} + {\left(1\right)}^{2} - 0\right) = 1J$.

$h = \dfrac{2{v}^{2}}{5g}$

questions.q: A force acts on a $2kg$ object so that its position is given as a function of time as $x = 3{t}^{2} + 5 .$ What is the work done by this force in first $5$ seconds?
questions.solution:
Here, the position of the object is $x = 3{t}^{2} + 5$, therefore the velocity of the object will be,

$v = \dfrac{d x}{d t} = \dfrac{d \left(3{t}^{2} + 5\right)}{d t}$

$v = 6t + 0$

From the work-energy theorem, all the work done by the force acting on it will be equal to the change in its kinetic energy, i.e.,

$W = KE\left(t = 5s\right) - KE\left(t = 0s\right)$
$W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times {\left(6 \times 5\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times {\left(6 \times 0\right)}^{2}$
$W = 900J$.

questions.q: A person trying to lose weight by burning fat lifts a mass of 10 kg upto a height of 1m 1000 times. Assume that the potential energy lost each time he lowers the mass is dissipated. How much fat will he use up considering the work done only when the weight is lifted up? questions.solution:
$m = 10kg, h = 1m, 1000times$

$= 10 \times 1 \times 9.8 = 98J$

$= 1000 \times 98$

$= 9.8 \times {10}^{4}J$

$= 7.6 \times {10}^{6}J$ per kg

$m = \dfrac{9.8 \times {10}^{4}}{7.6 \times {10}^{6}} = 1.289 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$= 12.89 \times {10}^{- 3}kg$

questions.q: A particle is moving in a circle of radius $r$ under the action of a force $F = \alpha{r}^{2}$ which is directed towards centre of the circle. Total mechanical energy (kinetic energy + potential energy) of the particle is (take potential energy$= 0$ for $r = 0$):
questions.solution:
Force $F = \alpha{r}^{2}$ will act as centripetal force

$⇒ \alpha{r}^{2} = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{r} ⇒ m{v}^{2} = \alpha{r}^{3}$

$∴$ Kinetic energy $K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

$⇒ K . E . = \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{2}$

Also $dU = - \overset{\to}{F} . d\overset{\to}{r}$

$∆ U = - ∫ \overset{\to}{F} . d\overset{\to}{r}$

$= - ∫ \alpha{r}^{2}\left(- dr\right)$

$= \alpha\mathop{∫}_{0}^{r}{r}^{2}dr$

$U - 0 = \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{3}$

$⇒ U = \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{3}$

So total mechanical energy

$E = U + K$

$= \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{2}$

$E = \dfrac{5\alpha{r}^{3}}{6}$

questions.q: A block of mass $m = 10kg$ rests on a horizontal table. The coefficient of friction between the block and the table is $0 . 05$. When hit by a bullet of mass $50g$ moving with speed $v$, that gets embedded in it, the block moves and comes to stop after moving a distance of $2m$ on the table. If a freely falling object were to acquire speed $\dfrac{v}{10}$ after being dropped from height $H$, then neglecting energy losses and taking $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$, the value of $H$ is close to
questions.solution:
By the conservation of linear momentum,

${m}_{1}v = \left(m + {m}_{1}\right){v}_{1}$

$⇒ {v}_{1} = \dfrac{{m}_{1}v}{m + {m}_{1}} . . . ( 1 )$

After collision by work energy theorem, we have

${W}_{friction} = ∆ k$

$⇒ - \mu\left(m + {m}_{1}\right)gx = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(m + {m}_{1}\right){v}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ \mugx = \dfrac{1}{2}{v}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ 0.05 \times 10 \times 2 = \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(\dfrac{{m}_{1}v}{m + {m}_{1}}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{5}{100} \times 10 \times 4 = {\left(\dfrac{50}{1000}\right)}^{2} \times \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{{\left(10 + \dfrac{50}{1000}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ 2 = \dfrac{1}{400}\dfrac{{v}^{2} \times 400}{{\left(201\right)}^{2}}$

${v}^{2} = {\left(201\right)}^{2}2$

$v = \sqrt{2} \times 201$

For a freely falling body,

$v ' = \sqrt{2gH}$

$\dfrac{v}{10} = \sqrt{2gH}$

$\dfrac{\sqrt{2} \times 201}{10} = \sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{gH}$

$\dfrac{{\left(201\right)}^{2}}{100} = 10H$

$H = \dfrac{{\left(201\right)}^{2}}{1000} = 40m$

$= 0.04km$

questions.q: A block of mass $m = 0.1kg$ is connected to a spring of unknown spring constant k. It is compressed to a distance $x$ from its equilibrium position and released from rest. After approaching half the distance $\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ from the equilibrium position, it hits another block and comes to rest momentarily, while the other block moves with velocity $3m{s}^{- 1}$. The total initial energy of the spring is:
questions.solution:
By mechanical energy conservation between compression positions $x$ and $\dfrac{x}{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}k{x}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}k{\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}k{x}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}k\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}k{x}^{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k{x}^{2}}{4m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{m}}\dfrac{x}{2}$

On collision with a block at rest

$∵$ Velocities are exchanged $⇒$ elastic collision between identical masses.

$∴ v = 3 = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{m}}\dfrac{x}{2}$

$⇒ 6 = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{m}}x$

$⇒ x = 6\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{3k}}$

$∴$ The initial energy of the spring is

$U = \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}k \times 36\dfrac{m}{3k} = 6m$

$U = 6 \times 0.1 = 0 .6 J$

Initial speed at point A, $u=v_0$
Speed at point $\mathrm{B}, v=$ ?

&=$\frac{v_0^2}{2 \mu g}+\frac{2 g h}{2 \mu g}=\frac{h}{\mu}+\frac{v_0^2}{2 \mu g}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body is moved along a straight line by a machine delivering a constant power. The distance moved by the body in time ' $t$ ' is proportional to

Power $=$ F. V

questions.q: A spring of force constant $800 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ has an extension of $5 \mathrm{~cm}$. The work done is extending it from $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ to $15 \mathrm{~cm}$ is
questions.solution: $\mathrm{W}=\int_{x_1}^{x_2} F d x=\int_{x_1}^{x_2} K x d x=K\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{x_1}^{x_2}=\frac{K}{2}\left[x_2^2-x_1^2\right]=\frac{800}{2}\left[(0.15)^2-(0.05)^2\right]=8 \mathrm{~J}$
